insight.title: How the light beneath our feet shapes your world
insight.subtitle: A quiet dance of glass and pulses connecting every moment

sections.text: Our world is held together by threads of glass. Beneath the concrete and under the salt of the deep ocean, billions of tiny light pulses race through hair-thin fibers. They carry every message you send and every memory you share. While the sky feels like the source of magic, the true power lives in the silent ground.

Instead of slow electricity, we use the speed of pure light. Think of it as a Morse code made of flashes, bouncing off the inside of glass tubes without ever escaping. This sequence of brightness creates the digital world. It is a tireless, luminous river flowing quietly through the dark earth.

This invisible net turns your morning routine into a global symphony. When you tap a screen, you aren’t just touching glass; you are reaching across continents in an eye-blink. Distance has become a choice rather than a barrier. We have replaced the physical weight of paper with the weightless speed of the sun.
We are no longer limited by where we stand, but by where we choose to look.

news.title: Israel bombs Sharif University of Technology in Iran, triggers gas outage; video shows aftermath
news.description: Middle East News: US-Israel airstrikes struck Tehran early Monday, hitting the Sharif University of Technology and causing gas outages in parts of the capital, Iranian .
news.why: Major strikes on energy infrastructure could lead to higher global fuel prices.

news.title: Asian markets gain while oil prices keep rising
news.description: Asian markets that are open for trading are mostly rising as investors continue to closely watch the war in Iran, soaring oil prices and what President Donald Trump might say next.
news.why: Rising oil prices mean you will likely pay more to commute soon.

news.title: Qatar’s LNG Tankers Idle Across Asia as Export Plant Stays Shut
news.description: More than four-dozen empty Qatari liquefied natural gas tankers are idling across Asia, as the nation’s export plant remains shut and the Strait of Hormuz largely closed because of the war in the Middle East.
news.why: Idle gas tankers may lead to significantly higher electricity and heating bills.

news.title: New Research Raises Kidney Concerns for Widely Used Cholesterol Medication

news.why: This common heart medication might increase your risk of developing kidney issues.

news.title: $15 billion investment: Google to kick off data centre project on April 28
news.description: So far, Google and its subsidiaries have data centres in 11 countries - the United States, Taiwan, Japan, Singapore, Ireland, the Netherlands, Denmark, Finland, Germany, Belgium, and Chile, spread across 29 geographic locations. The data centre cluster in Visakhapatnam is expected to be Asia's largest.
news.why: This massive technology investment will likely create many new high-paying jobs.

news.title: ASEAN at a Crossroads: Pathways for Deeper Economic Integration
news.description: This paper argues that the persistence of modest intra-ASEAN integration reflects structural constraints that trade liberalization initiatives alone cannot resolve.
news.why: Removing trade barriers could make everyday goods cheaper across Southeast Asia.

news.title: China Flies World's First Megawatt Hydrogen Turboprop Engine
news.description: The 16-minute unmanned test flight in Hunan Province marks what developers call a milestone in zero-emission aviation technology.
news.why: New hydrogen flight technology could eventually reduce the cost of air travel.

news.title: NASA Artemis II Astronauts Race Into Moon’s Embrace After Quiet Easter
news.description: Ahead of a lunar flyby on Monday, the crew celebrated the astronaut Jeremy Hansen’s first spaceflight and got a special message from Charlie Duke, the Apollo 16 moonwalker.
news.why: Lunar missions help secure more reliable global communication and navigation services.
